gb_1901.source: Statistical Abstract table21 p52, PDF61; image work/uk-rates-1901.png

france_1900.source: Andre and Delorme1973 tableII-1 PDF79, amounts in millions of new-franc equivalents converted at100; output Andersson Brambor v3.0 year1900

gaps: GB 1822 covers poor rates only; France uses a partial nearby-year estimate; US states use an 1820 benchmark. No separate New York 1822 income estimate established.

france_1822.coverage: Partial nearby-year comparison: net 1823 octrois plus selected 1826 local surtaxes. Not a complete 1822 local-tax total. Fixed departmental centimes are not separately added. Some departmental taxes appear in central accounts; do not assume central and local rows are additive.

us_states_1820.coverage: US state governments collectively; includes non-tax receipts; excludes federal and municipal revenue. Nearby-year benchmark, not a reconstructed 1822 observation.
us_states_1820.revenue_source: John Joseph Wallis (2000), American Government Finance in the Long Run: 1790 to 1990, Journal of Economic Perspectives 14(1), table 1 p65.
us_states_1820.gdp_source: Andersson and Brambor, Financing the State v3.0; United States 1820 gdpnom=703 million USD. Numerator and denominator both 1820.
us_states_1820.precision: Revenue total is calculated from rounded per-capita estimate; not an exact account total.

us_state_local_1902.denominator: GNP; percentages reported directly by source
us_state_local_1902.coverage: US state and local government revenue, including non-tax receipts; federal revenue excluded.
us_state_local_1902.source: John Joseph Wallis (2000), American Government Finance in the Long Run: 1790 to 1990, table 1 p65
